title: Variant resolution deadlock from policy timer mismatch and cross-region reroute
creator: Ava Chen
summary: During a planned capacity shift on 2026-03-10 we observed a sustained spike in 5xx errors and latency for multi-region customers. Smart routing entered a deadlock where requests repeatedly bounced between eu-west and us-east while attempting to resolve a compatible model variant. The immediate cause was a mismatch between the routing policy TTL and the variant resolution timer combined with an experimental flag that allowed 'best-effort' variant coercion. This created a state where no region accepted the request because each attempted a fallback that the other rejected.
timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Autoscaler initiated capacity shift off a maintenance host in eu-west; traffic gradually increased to other nodes.
2026-03-10 09:24 UTC - Latency and 5xx alarms for eu-west on Console; first alert routed to on-call infra SREs.
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Smart routing policy started TTL refresh loop; variant resolution requests showed increased retries in tracing.
2026-03-10 09:35 UTC - Cross-region reroutes observed; many requests bounced between eu-west and us-east for >20s.
2026-03-10 09:42 UTC - Incident declared; traffic throttles engaged and short-term manual override to prefer us-east applied.
2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Canary rollback of the experimental 'best-effort variant coercion' flag; error rate began to decline.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Full mitigation: routing policy TTL adjusted and hard-fallback patch deployed to stop oscillation.
2026-03-11 14:00 UTC - Preliminary root-cause analysis completed; engineering triage created this ticket for action items and follow-ups.
root_cause: A mismatch between routing policy TTL (configured at 5s) and the variant resolution timer (configured at 1s) allowed repeated variant-resolution attempts before the routing policy could mark a route as failed. An experimental best-effort coercion path attempted to substitute incompatible quantized model variants across regions. The coercion logic lacked compatibility checks for quantization profile metadata, causing both regions to reject the other’s fallback and enter a request reshuffle loop. In short: timer mismatch + permissive coercion + missing compatibility guard = deadlock.
impact: Multi-region customers experienced increased latency and ~12% elevation in 5xx errors for 40 minutes. Customer-facing dashboards showed degraded throughput for chat endpoints. Several high-volume customers reported degraded UX; one customer escalated to Support and required manual traffic steering.
mitigation: Short-term: rolled back the experimental coercion flag, applied a manual routing preference to us-east, and increased routing TTL to 15s to prevent rapid re-evaluation. Long-term: deployed a compatibility gate to validate quantization profiles before allowing cross-variant coercion and added a circuit-breaker to stop oscillation after 3 cross-region retries.
action_items: Add compatibility validation for quantization/profile metadata before allowing variant coercion (owner: Rina Gupta, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-24
Align default timers: standardize routing policy TTL and variant resolution timer via runtime config; add a validation test (owner: Marcus Patel, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-18
Implement exponential backoff + capped retries for cross-region fallback to avoid rapid oscillation (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-22
Instrument routing decision path with telemetry for variant compatibility checks and a new debug flag that can be safely toggled in production (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-20
Create a small runbook for Support/SREs to handle similar oscillation incidents and include safe manual overrides (owner: Support Docs, estimate: 2) - due 2026-03-17
Add end-to-end test in staging that simulates capacity shifts and verifies fallback behavior across quantized and FP16 variants (owner: QA, estimate: 4) - due 2026-03-25
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for quantization metadata compatibility - merged in PR 3521
Integration test that replays the incident trace with injected delays to ensure CBT (circuit-breaker) triggers - planned for staging
Chaos test: orchestrate node drains in eu-west while running mixed-variant traffic in staging to validate TTL/backoff defaults
postmortem_notes: Decisions: 1) Disable permissive variant coercion by default; opt-in via gated experiments only after compatibility validation. 2) Standardize critical timers in a shared config module to avoid mismatches in future. 3) Add a 'fallback circuit-breaker' to terminate oscillation. Trade-offs: increasing routing TTL reduces responsiveness to real failures; mitigations require careful tuning and additional telemetry. Follow-ups prioritized by customer impact and release window; compatibility guard is P0, circuit-breaker P0, TTL alignment P1.
